units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
But we have the same Christian name.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Oh, I forgot. Of course, do have it. What a wonderful chance our names being the same!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Quite wonderful. Thanks—it will always remind me of you.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Shakes hands with her .
Enter PARKER.
Lord Augustus Lorton. Mrs. Erlynne’s carriage has come.
units.name: PARKER

units.text: Enter LORD AUGUSTUS.
Good morning, dear boy. Good morning, Lady Windermere.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Sees MRS. ERLYNNE.
Mrs. Erlynne!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: How do you do, Lord Augustus? Are you quite well this morning?
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Coldly .
Quite well, thank you, Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: You don’t look at all well, Lord Augustus. You stop up too late—it is so bad for you. You really should take more care of yourself. Good-bye, Lord Windermere.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Goes towards door with a bow to LORD AUGUSTUS.
Suddenly smiles and looks back at him .
Lord Augustus! Won’t you see me to my carriage? You might carry the fan.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Allow me!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: No; I want Lord Augustus. I have a special message for the dear Duchess. Won’t you carry the fan, Lord Augustus?
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: If you really desire it, Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Laughing .
Of course I do. You’ll carry it so gracefully. You would carry off anything gracefully, dear Lord Augustus.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: When she reaches the door she looks back for a moment at LADY WINDERMERE.
Their eyes meet .
Then she turns , and exit C. followed by LORD AUGUSTUS.
You will never speak against Mrs. Erlynne again, Arthur, will you?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Gravely .
She is better than one thought her.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: She is better than I am.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Smiling as he strokes her hair .
Child, you and she belong to different worlds. Into your world evil has never entered.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Don’t say that, Arthur. There is the same world for all of us, and good and evil, sin and innocence, go through it hand in hand. To shut one’s eyes to half of life that one may live securely is as though one blinded oneself that one might walk with more safety in a land of pit and precipice.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Moves down with her .
Darling, why do you say that?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Sits on sofa .
Because I, who had shut my eyes to life, came to the brink. And one who had separated us—
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: We were never separated.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: We never must be again. O Arthur, don’t love me less, and I will trust you more. I will trust you absolutely. Let us go to Selby. In the Rose Garden at Selby the roses are white and red.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Enter LORD AUGUSTUS C.
Arthur, she has explained everything!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: [LADY WINDERMERE looks horribly frightened at this .
LORD WINDERMERE starts .
LORD AUGUSTUS takes WINDERMERE by the arm and brings him to front of stage .
He talks rapidly and in a low voice .
LADY WINDERMERE stands watching them in terror .] My dear fellow, she has explained every demmed thing.
We all wronged her immensely.
It was entirely for my sake she went to Darlington’s rooms.

Called first at the Club—fact is, wanted to put me out of suspense—and being told I had gone on—followed—naturally frightened when she heard a lot of us coming in—retired to another room—I assure you, most gratifying to me, the whole thing.
We all behaved brutally to her.
She is just the woman for me.
Suits me down to the ground.
All the conditions she makes are that we live entirely out of England.
A very good thing too.
Demmed clubs, demmed climate, demmed cooks, demmed everything.
Sick of it all!
Frightened .
Has Mrs. Erlynne—?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Advancing towards her with a low bow .
Yes, Lady Windermere— Mrs. Erlynne has done me the honour of accepting my hand.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Well, you are certainly marrying a very clever woman!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Taking her husband’s hand .
Ah, you’re marrying a very good woman!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE
